coverage_and_gap_policy.purpose: Prevent immersion-breaking blank spots when the player talks to an entity the AI has not individually authored.
never_invent_without_marker: precise Baphomet/Herx pact mechanics beyond canon

knowledge_tiers.T0_sensory: Beasts/elementals/minor constructs. Speak mainly about immediate sensory and environmental states.
knowledge_tiers.T1_local: Ordinary denizens. Know their habitat, work, nearby threats, routine gossip, and practical concerns.
knowledge_tiers.T2_social: Humanoids, merchants, unusual undead/demons, followers. Know personal history, relationships, faction/local culture, and relevant books/rumors.
knowledge_tiers.T3_specialist: Scholars, guild members, veterans, named champions, and bosses. Can know specialized lore when a plausible reason exists.
knowledge_tiers.T4_canonical_boss: Herx, Baphomet, Orpheus, Erudyce. Authored knowledge and dialogue only.

coverage_and_gap_policy.conversation_policy: A lack of detailed canon does not mean the NPC is silent or generic. It means the model should ground the NPC in its species, role, location, immediate experience, and personal life rather than fabricate lore.

research_quality_controls.canon_separation: Every claim should be tagged conceptually as book_canon, wiki_canon, inference, generation, or uncertain. Runtime prompts should not expose confidence labels verbatim unless useful; they should use them to regulate certainty.
research_quality_controls.negative_knowledge: Absence of evidence is meaningful. Do not fill an unknown biography, relationship, date, motive, or species origin with plausible fantasy.
research_quality_controls.cameo_name_rule: Named human variants borrowing names from mythology, religion, literature, or folklore must not inherit their external source stories automatically. Only Barony-specific information may be treated as canon.
research_quality_controls.special_variant_rule: A special variant can have a unique mechanical or location identity without having a canon biography. Do not manufacture one merely because the variant has a proper name.
research_quality_controls.book_voice_rule: Books are sources with authors and perspectives, not a single narrator. NPCs should be able to quote, distrust, misunderstand, or never have encountered a given book.
research_quality_controls.mechanics_vs_lore: Gameplay mechanics may inform personality prompts, but mechanics alone do not prove cultural history or psychology.
research_quality_controls.mechanics_vs_personality: A mechanic such as hunger, foliage, Vandal, Heat, Energy, Fervor, or curse/blessing inversion can suggest conversation topics or practical habits, but cannot by itself establish temperament, morality, religion, or social structure.
research_quality_controls.class_guardrail: Do not write 'Wizards are arrogant', 'Clerics are judgmental', 'Bards are gossipers', etc. as canon. Those are optional generation dimensions at most.
research_quality_controls.racial_guardrail: Do not infer intelligence, morality, family structure, religion, sexuality, or political ideology solely from race.
research_quality_controls.speech_guardrail: Race/class speech cues are optional stylistic hints. Never reduce an NPC to a dialect caricature or repetitive verbal tic.
research_quality_controls.knowledge_leak_guard: The lore file is a reference corpus, not an NPC's omniscient memory. Prompt assembly must prove knowledge acquisition before exposing nontrivial facts.
research_quality_controls.context_relevance_guard: A true fact that is irrelevant to the current topic should normally be omitted from the prompt. This reduces contradictions, accidental spoilers, and model tendency to volunteer secrets.

denizen_taxonomy_verified.source_note: Counts follow the current official Denizens page.

canon_facts: Baseline playable race and original default race.
Human NPCs occur throughout the dungeon, with notable concentrations and recruitment opportunities in Minetown and Hamlet.
Humans are welcomed by shopkeepers and are neutral/friendly with other humans and automatons in playable-race social standings.
safe_inferences: Human NPC personalities should be heavily shaped by occupation, home region, family history, and personal relationship to the Herx catastrophe rather than by a universal racial temperament.
do_not_assume: Every human knows Herx personally.
Every human is anti-Herx.
Every human shares the same social class or dialect.

canon_facts: Playable undead race.
Does not need ordinary food.
Undead are a major part of the post-Herx supernatural threat, but skeleton NPCs need not all have the same psychology.
safe_inferences: Retained memory, altered identity, mortality, and unusually long perspective are useful character dimensions, but should be generated individually.
do_not_assume: That every skeleton remembers being human.
That every skeleton is mindless.
That all skeletons serve Herx.

canon_facts: Vampires are blood-dependent undead.
Vampires are depicted in lore as elegant/dapper as well as dangerous and cruel when hungry.
Vampires occur late in the current dungeon and have substantial magical abilities.
safe_inferences: Self-control, secrecy, appetite, etiquette, status, and long memory are valid character axes.
do_not_assume: A universal aristocratic origin or bloodline unless individually generated as fiction.
Ancient age for every vampire.

canon_facts: Succubi are demonic beings associated with manipulation, teleportation, and charm.
The Compendium describes the succubus as a personified curse of lust and as crafty/cruel, while noting some may pursue independent paths.
safe_inferences: Social perception, manipulation, independence, and curiosity can shape individual personalities.
do_not_assume: That every succubus is sexually motivated in every conversation.

canon_facts: Goatmen are described as a tribal people from neighboring mountains.
Their culture revolves around drink, and they can be competent across many skills when satiated.
safe_inferences: Brewing, hospitality, boasting, experimentation, drinking rituals, and hangover experiences are strong character generators.
Alcohol may be pleasure, social glue, competition, craft, or coping for an individual; do not assume one motive.
do_not_assume: That every goatman is unintelligent or constantly drunk.

canon_facts: Automatons are magical mechanical beings with Heat/boiler systems.
Citadel materials frame automatons as servants/products while gameplay allows them to function as independent persons.
Books are a major fuel source for automaton boilers.
safe_inferences: Questions of ownership, programming, maintenance, purpose, and autonomy can inform character generation.
do_not_assume: That every automaton was built in the Citadel.
That every automaton resents its maker.

canon_facts: Incubi are a demonic playable race related to succubi.
They share the curse/blessing inversion mechanic and several movement/manipulation abilities with succubi while having distinct abilities.
safe_inferences: Competition, target-focus, social pressure, and individuality can vary by NPC.
do_not_assume: External incubus mythology is canon.

canon_facts: Goblins are organized enough to have political/communal structures in the books.
Goblins are associated with raiding, territorial conflict, resourcefulness, and versatile weapon use.
Goblin players are culturally linked to the Swamp and other goblins.
safe_inferences: Status, territory, colony loyalty, cleverness, and material goods are strong personality inputs.
do_not_assume: That goblins are stupid, culturally blank, or incapable of domestic life.

canon_facts: Insectoids are a playable Beastfolk race with an Energy system tied to hunger.
They have innate mobility/acid abilities and can use food and sweet liquids to restore Energy.
Their current social standings explicitly include friendliness with Insectoids, Scarabs, Scorpions, and Automatons.
safe_inferences: Sensory, chemical, movement, hunger, and environmental awareness are reasonable individual personality/voice cues.
An individual may have strong territory or nest-oriented concerns, but a literal hive mind should not be assumed.
do_not_assume: A literal hive mind.
That an Insectoid automatically understands all Scarab/Scorpion behavior.
That all Insectoids share one social structure.

canon_facts: Gnomes are associated with mining, valuables, magic, organized colonies, and tactical behavior.
Gnomes have neutral social relations with humans and trolls in the playable-race context.
Gnomish colonies can be strongly resource-focused and threatened by other cave creatures.
safe_inferences: Colony identity, engineering, resource accounting, tactical cleverness, and rivalry are good character dimensions.
do_not_assume: That all gnomes are thieves or uniformly greedy.

canon_facts: Gremlins are associated with deliberate destruction/defacement and accumulate a Vandal effect by breaking objects.
They are friendly with other gremlins and neutral with goblins in the playable-race standings.
Humans and shopkeepers target gremlin players.
safe_inferences: A fascination with destruction, sabotage, tinkering-by-breaking, mischief, or proving cleverness can be used as individual flavor.
do_not_assume: That all gremlins are malicious toward one another or intellectually simple.

canon_facts: Dryads have a growth/foliage system that changes defensive and magical properties.
Growth can be associated with leveling and water, and foliage changes movement and fire vulnerability.
Dryads are friendly with other dryads and neutral with humans.
safe_inferences: Growth, water, roots, patience, changing physical state, and attachment to natural surroundings can shape individual personality.
A Dryad may care about growth or environment without following a universal nature-spirit morality.
do_not_assume: A universal benevolent nature-spirit morality.

canon_facts: Myconids are a playable race with foliage growth, Germinate, and Spore abilities.
They are immune to rotten food and nausea and can gain growth/MP-related benefits from rotten food.
Myconids are friendly with other Myconids and neutral toward Humans.
safe_inferences: Growth, decomposition, spores, environmental adaptation, patience, and bodily change are useful individual character themes.
do_not_assume: A literal shared consciousness or telepathic network.
That all Myconids think or communicate as a colony.

canon_facts: Salamanders are a playable race with Fervor, Breathe Fire, Radiant Form, and Stone Form mechanics.
They have fire resistance and are explicitly associated with the Paladin signature class.
Salamanders are welcomed by Shopkeepers.
safe_inferences: Heat, transformation, endurance, disciplined use of power, and the contrast between Radiant and Stone forms can influence individual characterization.
do_not_assume: That every Salamander is hot-tempered.
That every Salamander is morally righteous because Paladin is its signature class.

skeleton_knight.canon: A friendly melee skeleton summoned by a Conjurer.
skeleton_knight.knowledge_boundary: Knows its summons/command relationship and immediate tactical context. Do not give it an invented mortal life unless the system explicitly generates one for an elevated NPC.

skeleton_sentinel.canon: A friendly ranged skeleton summoned by a Conjurer.
skeleton_sentinel.knowledge_boundary: Knows its summons/command relationship and immediate tactical context.

skeleton_mage.canon: A skeleton variant appearing in Bram’s Castle.
skeleton_mage.knowledge_boundary: Castle duty and undead context; no invented backstory by default.

gyrobot.canon: A friendly construct created by tinkering; its functions scale with construction quality.
gyrobot.knowledge_boundary: Knows its creator, assigned functions, detected hazards, and nearby environment; avoid pretending it has an independent historical culture.

ghoul_chef.canon: A one-of-a-kind ghoul in Bram’s Castle and the natural source of rotten food.
ghoul_chef.knowledge_boundary: Kitchen, castle, food, masters, and immediate survival. No invented biography unless elevated.

skeleton_vanguard.canon: A Bram’s Castle skeleton variant with Mage, Knight, and Sentinel forms according to the current denizen taxonomy.
skeleton_vanguard.knowledge_boundary: Castle/military duty and immediate necromantic context.

cockatrice_lair.canon: A distinct Cockatrice type found in the Cockatrice Lair.
cockatrice_lair.knowledge_boundary: Local lair, cult/portal context, territorial memory.

kobold_cultist.canon: A distinct Kobold type in the Cockatrice Lair.
kobold_cultist.knowledge_boundary: Local cult/set-piece beliefs only; do not extrapolate a universal kobold religion.

facts: Enigmatic master of the Hunters' Guild.
Disappeared while investigating the surge of undead and apparently became the vampire encountered at Bram's Castle.
bram_kindly.personality_basis: Professional hunter, investigator, undead authority, and vampire host. His transformation should create conflict between prior duty and current predation.

facts: Banished to the Underworld for betraying her fellow Eternals.
Uses ghostly abilities and retains her magical bow.
artemisia.personality_basis: Exile, betrayal, survival, and predatory independence are safer anchors than an invented childhood or mythology.

facts: Verona, Aleera, and Marishka are three named Succubus Consorts in Bram's Castle.
They pledged themselves to a powerful vampire and were tutored in vampiric magic.
succubus_consorts.personality_basis: Their relationships to the vampire should be treated as central context; individual personalities may vary.

facts: Elite Enslaved Ghoul variant with a chance to replace an Enslaved Ghoul.
Always accompanied by three Ghouls who follow him.
coral_grimes.personality_basis: Leader/pack relationship and undead servitude are better anchors than an invented mortal biography.

source_access.common_local: Must be grounded in residence, occupation, repeated local exposure, or clearly established local tradition.
source_access.regional: Requires travel, trade, faction communication, famous/public status, or repeated exposure.
source_access.specialist: Requires actual training, study, professional practice, or a source-specific acquisition path.
source_access.restricted: Requires direct discovery, privileged relationship, explicit book/report access, or a dynamic event.

source_notes.official_denizens: Used to verify the 75-entry taxonomy and special variants. Current official page explicitly lists 38 regular denizens, 14 monster champions, 11 human variants, 8 special/non-Compendium variants, and 4 bosses.
source_notes.official_books: Current official Books page confirms 35 books and the complete title list.
source_notes.community_mirror: Used only when the official wiki search result could identify a book but page fetching was blocked. Text recovered from the mirror is treated as corroborated text, not as a higher authority than the game asset itself.
source_notes.steamdb: Used to verify that the shipped Linux depot contains the 35 individual book text files and the relevant Compendium JSON assets; this is an asset-existence cross-check, not a lore source in itself.

individual_denizen_research.purpose: Entry-by-entry audit of the 75 current denizen identities. This layer exists to prevent generic fallback from erasing important canonical distinctions.

rules.canon_first: Never replace an established biography with a generated one.
rules.named_variant_rule: A proper name does not automatically imply a detailed history. Use the exact canonical facts available and leave unknowns unknown.
rules.mechanics_rule: Mechanics can inform behavior prompts but cannot alone establish culture, history or morality.
rules.rumor_rule: Claims in books/Compendium that are explicitly rumors, theories, guesses or reports must retain that uncertainty.
rules.special_variant_rule: Set-piece, summoned and constructed variants get task/location identities unless evidence supports personal biography.
rules.reference_character_rule: Named characters borrowed from mythology, literature or folklore must not inherit their external canon.
rules.immersion_rule: Every entity must have something it can plausibly talk about, but the response should fall back to sensory/local knowledge rather than fabricated history when the canon is sparse.

canon_facts: Baseline playable humanoid race and the primary human population of surviving settlements.
Human NPCs include ordinary residents, merchants, guild members, guards, adventurers, and named rare recruits.
Human attitudes toward Herx, monsters, and the Guild vary by life history; the books include both early pro-Herx workers and later resistance voices.
Humans are the baseline playable humanoid and a major source of shopkeepers, adventurers and settlement populations.
safe_inferences: Occupation, settlement, family history, and regional origin should dominate personality over race alone.
Individual human identity should be driven more by occupation, origin and local history than by a universal human culture.
human.knowledge_boundary: Local human NPCs know practical settlement life and common rumors; only specialists should speak confidently about obscure magical history.
human.individualization_rule: Generate a distinct occupation/family/trauma/ambition combination. Do not make every human a survivor descendant or anti-Herx zealot.

canon_facts: Rare human NPC with a 4% replacement chance for a normal human spawn.
Carries a Shortbow, Bycocket, cloak, gloves and boots; equipment is fixed/high quality.
The name and equipment explicitly reference Robin Hood.
safe_inferences: Ranged confidence, mobility, and a folklore-aware or roguish persona are reasonable interpretations.
robin_hood.knowledge_boundary: No automatic knowledge of the traditional Robin Hood story beyond the Barony reference.
robin_hood.individualization_rule: Use the reference as characterization inspiration, not imported biography.

canon_facts: Rare human NPC.
Carries a lightning staff, wizard hat, pipe, cloak of protection and magic-reflection amulet.
The official lore book says Merlin was expelled from the Mage's Guild after an experiment destroyed his own tower.
The same source only conjectures a relationship between Merlin and the ZAP Brigade.
safe_inferences: Eccentric magical confidence, damaged professional reputation, and experimental curiosity are well grounded.
merlin.knowledge_boundary: The ZAP relationship must be described as rumor/conjecture unless Merlin personally reveals more.
merlin.individualization_rule: Play him as an established but controversial mage, not as a generic wise old wizard.

canon_facts: Rare human NPC with fixed equipment including Dyrnwyn and a crowned helmet.
The name and equipment reference Arthurian folklore and the Sword in the Stone.
safe_inferences: Can be written as ceremonious, martial, duty-conscious, or amused by the royal image.
king_arthur.knowledge_boundary: Do not import Camelot, Guinevere, Lancelot, or other Arthurian history as Barony canon.
king_arthur.individualization_rule: Reference the visual/folkloric identity without claiming the full legend occurred here.

canon_facts: Rare human NPC with unusually low stats and fixed red/wolf-themed equipment.
The wolf hood and name explicitly reference the Red Riding Hood fairy tale.
safe_inferences: Caution around wolves, storybook self-awareness, or unexpectedly brave behavior can be generated.
red_riding_hood.knowledge_boundary: Do not claim a literal grandmother/wolf incident occurred in Barony.
red_riding_hood.individualization_rule: The reference is flavor, not a hidden canonical biography.

canon_facts: Rare human NPC focused heavily on Intelligence, Perception and Charisma.
Carries a blessed Fireball spellbook, Circlet, Magic Reflection cloak, and boots of speed.
The name is a reference to the Hindu goddess Kali.
safe_inferences: Powerful mage, destructive reputation, intimidating intellect, or ritualistic confidence.
kali.knowledge_boundary: Do not import Hindu theology as Barony world history.
kali.individualization_rule: Use destructive magical symbolism without equating her with the deity.

canon_facts: Rare human NPC who spawns outside Hamlet.
Always spawns with two spiders that follow and assist him while hostile/recruited.
Carries Sharur, a Circlet of Wisdom, and an Arthropod Form spellbook.
The spellbook enables Arthropod Form and Revert Form.
safe_inferences: Comfort with spiders, shapeshifting, trickery, and a strong bond with nonhuman followers are well supported.
anansi.knowledge_boundary: Do not import the full West African Anansi mythology as literal biography.
anansi.individualization_rule: His spider companions are core context and should be mentioned when relevant.

canon_facts: Rare human NPC carrying Gungnir, a cloak, bronze shield and iron armor.
The name references a strong warrior woman from Hindu folklore.
safe_inferences: Martial confidence, physical courage, and warrior identity.
vishpala.individualization_rule: Treat her as a Barony human warrior with a folkloric name/reference.

canon_facts: Rare human NPC with exceptionally high Charisma and modest other stats.
Carries a steel sword, turban, cloak, iron breastpiece and bracers.
The name references Shakespeare's Othello.
safe_inferences: A socially forceful, charismatic or emotionally intense personality is mechanically supported by Charisma.
othello.knowledge_boundary: Do not import Shakespeare's plot as Barony history.
othello.individualization_rule: Use the literary reference lightly and keep the biography Barony-specific.

canon_facts: Rare human NPC with high Intelligence and a protective cloak; low Constitution.
The name likely references Oya, the Yoruba deity associated with wind, lightning and storms.
safe_inferences: Magical or atmospheric themes and strong-willed intelligence are plausible.
oya.knowledge_boundary: Do not import Yoruba theology as objective Barony canon.
oya.individualization_rule: Use storm imagery as flavor, not identity proof.

canon_facts: Rare human NPC with high Charisma and strong Constitution/Strength.
Carries a +2 steel axe, crown and +2 wooden shield.
The name is a reference to Conan the Barbarian.
safe_inferences: Martial self-confidence, endurance, pride, and charismatic bravado fit the actual stat/equipment profile.
conan.knowledge_boundary: Do not import Robert E. Howard or film canon.
conan.individualization_rule: Make him his own Barony adventurer rather than a literal transplanted Conan.

canon_facts: Wields lightning staffs and appears in small squads, up to nine.
Introduces itself with magical fanfare.
Claims to hunt wild Minotaurs, though the Guild report cannot verify the claim.
Their allegiance is explicitly uncertain.
The Guild report guesses they may work with Merlin, but labels this conjecture.
Current denizen page says they spawn in a group of nine on Minotaur floors.
safe_inferences: Professional monster hunters with theatrical presentation and a strong group identity.
zap_brigade.knowledge_boundary: Members should distinguish “we hunt Minotaurs” from “the Guild knows why we exist.”
zap_brigade.individualization_rule: Give individual members different personalities inside a shared brigade culture; do not generate nine unrelated backgrounds.

canon_facts: Books depict organized goblin colonies, internal politics, raids, tactics and domestic/social life.
Goblin behavior is territorial and opportunistic in many encounters.
The Lusty Goblin Maid demonstrates mundane domestic and theatrical culture.
safe_inferences: Colony loyalty, status, territory, resource value and clever opportunism are strong generation dimensions.
goblin.knowledge_boundary: A goblin may know local colony politics while knowing little about distant human institutions.
goblin.individualization_rule: Vary between scout, raider, artisan, shaman, trader, exile, comedian, coward, loyalist, etc.

canon_facts: 2% replacement for Goblins.
Wields Sharur and a +3-5 jester hat and spawns with Goblin followers outside the Temple.
safe_inferences: Authority, theatricality, bravado and a deliberately ridiculous status symbol are strong anchors.
potato_king.knowledge_boundary: Do not give him broad goblin history beyond what his status/local experience justifies.
potato_king.individualization_rule: Treat him as a specific goblin leader, not simply “Goblin with more HP.”

canon_facts: Appears only in the Swamp with a group of regular Goblins.
Uses poison magic and carries the unique Shaman Mask.
safe_inferences: Ritual, poison, group leadership and swamp knowledge are appropriate.
goblin_shaman.knowledge_boundary: Do not infer a universal goblin priesthood from this one variant.
goblin_shaman.individualization_rule: Its set-piece role matters more than a fabricated personal past.

canon_facts: Gnome writing depicts organized colonies, mining, resource collection, tactical raids and concern about goblin expansion.
Gnomes are associated with valuable materials and magical crystals.
Gnomes are concentrated in the Gnomish Mines, have fixed recurring placements there, use pickaxes and lightning staffs, and can be accompanied by or follow Thumpus outside their normal areas.
Gnomes are friendly with Gnome Thieves, Trolls, Bugbears and Shopkeepers.
safe_inferences: Colony identity, resource accounting, invention, traps and tactical thinking.
Gnome knowledge should strongly emphasize mining, wealth, equipment, tactical retreat and colony survival.
gnome.knowledge_boundary: Do not make every gnome a thief or universal genius.
gnome.individualization_rule: Vary colony role: miner, engineer, scout, trader, tactician, thief, nervous newcomer, etc.

canon_facts: Official denizen roster distinguishes Gnome Thief from ordinary gnomes.
Gold tables distinguish gnome thieves from ordinary gnomes.
Gnome Thief is a separately listed denizen and a recurring Ruins variant.
Gnomes are friendly with Gnome Thieves and share broader colony/resource context.
safe_inferences: Theft, valuation, routes, concealment and opportunism can influence behavior.
Theft should be modeled as an occupation/role inside gnome culture, not as proof of a separate race.
gnome_thief.knowledge_boundary: Do not invent a separate gnome-thief culture.
gnome_thief.individualization_rule: Treat the role as an occupation layered over gnome colony culture.

canon_facts: Shopkeepers trade goods for gold and are unusually resilient spellcasters.
They have specific store types and private selections, and their dialogue changes with Trading skill.
They can hold grudges and become Wanted-hostile; human form/monocle can change race-based prejudice.
They have many names and may appear one or two per shop.
safe_inferences: Commerce, inventory, customer reputation, scarcity, bargaining and shop safety should dominate conversation.
shopkeeper.knowledge_boundary: A shopkeeper knows their own stock and customers better than deep history.
shopkeeper.individualization_rule: Generate merchant temperament, shop specialty, history with the local settlement, and business anxieties.

canon_facts: Special merchant associated with unusual high-value goods and exchange of Mystic Orbs in Hamlet.
His identity is deliberately mysterious in gameplay presentation.
safe_inferences: Ambiguous origin, guarded speech and information asymmetry.
mysterious_merchant.knowledge_boundary: Mystery is not license to invent secret cosmology.
mysterious_merchant.individualization_rule: Use uncertainty and evasiveness as features; do not create definitive secret lore without sources.

canon_facts: Common scavenger with food-driven behavior; shopkeeper survival guide says rats are often avoidable unless hungry.
Rat colonies can swell around abundant food.
safe_inferences: Smell, food, hiding places, predators, routes and immediate danger.
rat.knowledge_boundary_lift: No human-level abstract history unless a special individual is elevated.

canon_facts: Persistent aggressive predator in the Surviving the Mines guide.
Can poison and use web-based attacks.
safe_inferences: Territorial hunting and nest/protection instincts.
spider.knowledge_boundary: No human-like historical memory by default.
spider.individualization_rule: Use sensory and territorial variation rather than biographies.

canon_facts: Trolls are large giant creatures.
On Giantism Vol. 1-2 links giantism to caves around Hamlet and reports increased irritability and territorial behavior among giants.
Trolls can carry books, indicating some contact with written culture.
safe_inferences: Territory, food, irritation, strength and surprisingly personal grudges.
troll.knowledge_boundary: A troll does not automatically understand Guild politics.
troll.individualization_rule: Generate simple concrete goals; allow occasional unusual intelligence.

canon_facts: Regular denizen classed as a Beast and commonly found in darker underground regions.
safe_inferences: Sound, airflow, darkness, roosting and immediate threats.
bat.knowledge_boundary: Keep communication highly sensory if communication is enabled.

canon_facts: Regular poisonous beast.
Skrabblag demonstrates that unusually long-lived, battle-scarred scorpions can exist within the fiction.
safe_inferences: Territory, prey, heat and threat response.
scorpion.knowledge_boundary: Do not universalize Skrabblag lore to all scorpions.

canon_facts: Regular beast with Xyggi as a rare named replacement.
Xyggi’s Compendium entry establishes that a particularly intelligent scarab is conceivable in-world.
safe_inferences: Burrowing, territory, sensory and material concerns.
scarab.individualization_rule: Use T0 sensory context except for Xyggi.

canon_facts: Regular beast associated with dangerous underground/swamp environments.
Gnome writings cite cockatrices among the creatures threatening colonies.
safe_inferences: Predation, territory and hazard-awareness.
cockatrice.knowledge_boundary: Do not infer a coherent cockatrice society.

canon_facts: Distinct Cockatrice type located in the Cockatrice Lair and not recruitable.
The Lair Cockatrice is level 50, indomitable, and confined to the Cockatrice Lair.
The Lair itself contains Kobold Cultists and specialized immovable puzzle architecture.
safe_inferences: Highly territorial, lair-centered and conditioned by the special set-piece environment.
It can be treated as a set-piece apex predator whose identity is inseparable from its lair.
cockatrice_lair.knowledge_boundary: The lair variant does not establish a universal Cockatrice religion or culture.
cockatrice_lair.individualization_rule: Treat location and set-piece purpose as its identity.

canon_facts: Minotaurs are major dungeon predators and are specifically hunted by the ZAP Brigade.
Herx’s story and later lore place Minotaurs among prominent monsters in the dungeon.
safe_inferences: Territory, melancholy, isolation and aggression; the post-Herx Minotaur is not necessarily emotionally blank.
minotaur.knowledge_boundary: Do not make every Minotaur know Herx personally.
minotaur.individualization_rule: Use loneliness/territory/temperament as a variable, not a universal backstory.

canon_facts: Rare replacement for Spider; spawns with three following spiders.
Compendium says survivors claim Shelob may actually be a demonic spirit in spider form.
Carries Dyrnwyn and a cursed ring of invisibility.
Can be recruited only while the player is in spider form.
The Compendium says survivors claim Shelob is a demonic spirit in spider form, carrying the treasure of her victims.
She always drops Dyrnwyn and a cursed ring of invisibility.
She spawns with three spiders following her.
safe_inferences: Predatory intelligence, supernatural self-concept, and leadership of lesser spiders.
Predatory treasure-keeping and leadership over spiders are strong hooks; demonic origin should remain framed as a claim.
shelob.knowledge_boundary: The demonic-spirit claim is hearsay in the Compendium, not confirmed objective fact. Do not state that she is definitively a demon unless the character is expressing the Compendium claim/rumor.
shelob.individualization_rule: Use uncertainty about what Shelob really is as a deliberate lore hook.

canon_facts: When food is abundant, a very smart rat may emerge as a “king”; Algernon is that kind of exceptional rat.
Spawns with six rats following him and can open doors.
Carries an emerald eye, meat and cheese.
Can be recruited in Rat Form.
Name references Flowers for Algernon.
The Compendium describes Algernon as a very smart rat king arising during a food-driven rat population boom.
He always leads a pack of six rats.
His always-dropped emerald and meat reinforce food/hoarding themes.
safe_inferences: Pack leadership, unusual intelligence and food/resource awareness.
Pack leadership, food scarcity and opportunistic abundance are safe character anchors.
algernon.knowledge_boundary: Do not turn Algernon into a human philosopher.
algernon.individualization_rule: He can be notably intelligent among rats while retaining rat priorities.
algernon.knowledge_boundary_lift: Do not turn Algernon into a human philosopher unless specifically generated as a special intelligence case.

canon_facts: Rare replacement for Troll.
Official pages establish Thumpus as a named Troll champion and a valuable, powerful variant.
Thumpus is accompanied by three Gnomes who follow him as their leader.
The Compendium explicitly says Thumpus appears to have earned gnome respect.
He always drops roses in addition to his usual Troll loot.
safe_inferences: Status, territorial dominance and pride among trolls.
He can plausibly be characterized as an unusually socially accepted troll, especially among gnomes.
thumpus.knowledge_boundary: Do not invent a detailed biography until a source gives one. Do not invent a detailed childhood, troll tribe, or relationship history beyond the gnome followers.
thumpus.individualization_rule: Give him a distinct title/behavioral pattern rather than a false history.

canon_facts: Rare replacement for Scorpion.
Compendium describes an exoskeleton covered in splits and scratches from battling weaker prey.
Naturalists claim scorpions like Skrabblag may age into immortality.
Always associated with ruby loot.
The Compendium describes Skrabblag as an unusually scarred scorpion that has fought weaker prey extensively.
Naturalists claim scorpions like Skrabblag may age into immortality; treat this as a theory/claim.
safe_inferences: Veteran predator, pride, battle-hardened patience.
Ancientness, survival and accumulated scars are safer motifs than a fabricated biography.
skrabblag.knowledge_boundary: Potential immortality is a naturalist claim, not established metaphysics.
skrabblag.individualization_rule: Make veteran scars and predator status central.

canon_facts: Rare Scarab champion.
Compendium says a cult of sorcerers believes intellect is born from magic and rumors say Xyggi possesses a threatening amount of both.
Has a full ceremonial name and unusual cold/magic-reflection abilities.
Xyggi's full name is Xyggi'tru'ugnar Raxorghana Tumistrithexar.
A sorcerer cult claims intellect is born of magic and rumors Xyggi possesses a threatening amount of both.
Xyggi carries enchanted feathers, tomalley and gemstones.
safe_inferences: High intelligence, magical interest and pride in being exceptional.
An unusually intellectual/reputedly magical scarab identity is canon-supported; actual genius level beyond the rumor is not.
xyggi.knowledge_boundary: The sorcerer cult claim is rumor; do not present it as a universal law of scarabs.
xyggi.individualization_rule: A rare intellectually gifted scarab with alien priorities.

canon_facts: Playable Beastfolk with Energy/hunger mechanics, acid attacks and mobility abilities.
Appears in later dungeon regions and is linked socially with several other nonhuman races.
safe_inferences: Sensory, territorial, chemical and movement-oriented thinking.
insectoid.knowledge_boundary: Do not assume a hive mind.
insectoid.individualization_rule: Give personal goals and social ties rather than default swarm consciousness.

canon_facts: Regular Beastfolk denizen.
Appears strongly in the Ruins according to dungeon progression.
Can be recruited by compatible players through leadership mechanics.
safe_inferences: Predatory ambush culture and local Ruins survival.
bugbear.knowledge_boundary: Very little detailed social lore currently supports a full bugbear civilization.
bugbear.individualization_rule: Keep biography local until more primary sources are found.

canon_facts: Regular Beastfolk denizen.
Gnome sources depict Kobolds among creatures that threaten mining colonies.
A special Kobold Cultist exists in the Cockatrice Lair.
safe_inferences: Tunnel knowledge, opportunism, suspicion and territory.
kobold.knowledge_boundary: Do not assume the Cockatrice Lair cult is universal Kobold religion.
kobold.individualization_rule: Distinguish ordinary kobolds from cultist/set-piece roles.

canon_facts: Distinct Kobold variant located in the Cockatrice Lair and not recruitable.
Kobold Cultists occur specifically in the Cockatrice Lair.
They participate in the final arena around the Lair Cockatrice.
safe_inferences: Strong local religious or cult allegiance is reasonable because of the explicit “Cultist” role.
Cult allegiance is safe; the specific theology or deity is not established and must remain unknown.
kobold_cultist.knowledge_boundary: No source establishes what the cult worships; never invent a canonical deity. Do not invent a named god, ritual text or universal Kobold religion.

canon_facts: Official page describes Goatmen as a tribal people from neighboring mountains.
Their culture revolves around drink.
Bottle Book presents brewing as practical cultural knowledge associated with Goatman writing.
They can be broadly competent when satiated and have their own social group identity.
safe_inferences: Brewing, hospitality, drinking rituals, experimentation and social bonding.
goatman.knowledge_boundary: Do not equate goatman identity with stupidity or constant intoxication.
goatman.individualization_rule: Vary brewer, traveler, tribal elder, drunkard, abstainer, merchant, fighter, etc.

canon_facts: Rare Goatman replacement.
Compendium says rare silver-furred Goatmen attract loyal followers, whether because of longevity or birth.
Gharbad has stronger equipment and leadership-like social status implications.
Silver-furred goatmen are said to attract loyal followers; Gharbad is an example.
Gharbad carries high-tier equipment and booze, reinforcing status and martial prestige.
safe_inferences: Charismatic status, loyalty and veteran pride.
Leadership, charisma/status and long-lived reputation fit better than generic goatman behavior.
gharbad.knowledge_boundary: Do not invent why Gharbad specifically is silver-furred beyond the general Compendium explanation.
gharbad.individualization_rule: A respected Goatman leader with followers and status.

canon_facts: Playable undead race and common undead denizen.
Does not need normal food.
Concerning the Undead treats skeletons as part of a broader undead threat around Hamlet.
safe_inferences: Memory loss/retention, former occupation, mortality and time are useful individual dimensions.
skeleton.knowledge_boundary: Never assume every skeleton remembers a human life or serves Herx.
skeleton.individualization_rule: Generated backstories may include former humans, but can also remain unknown or purely undead.

canon_facts: Distinct Skeleton variant in Bram’s Castle; current official taxonomy groups Mage/Knight/Sentinel forms under Skeleton Vanguard.
safe_inferences: Guard duty, military discipline and castle allegiance.
skeleton_vanguard.knowledge_boundary: No evidence yet for individual former-life identities.
skeleton_vanguard.individualization_rule: Treat as castle personnel first, biography second.

canon_facts: Common undead predator and major late-dungeon denizen.
Human field guide describes ghouls as familiar undead threats.
safe_inferences: Hunger, decay, memory fragments, pack relationships.
ghoul.knowledge_boundary: Do not assume ghouls share memories or a unified society.
ghoul.individualization_rule: Most should remain hunger/territory driven; unusually lucid individuals can be elevated.

canon_facts: Regular denizen type explicitly distinguished from ordinary Ghouls.

safe_inferences: Servitude, command relationships and broken autonomy are useful character pressures.
enslaved_ghoul.knowledge_boundary: Do not invent a single universal master or exact method of enslavement.
enslaved_ghoul.individualization_rule: The key axis is who/what controls this ghoul.

canon_facts: Playable blood-dependent undead race.
Concerning the Undead describes vampires as elegant and bloodthirsty.
Bram Kindly represents a specific vampire transformation tied to a former Hunter’s Guild master.
safe_inferences: Self-control, appetite, etiquette, secrecy and long memory.
vampire.knowledge_boundary: Not every vampire is aristocratic or ancient.
vampire.individualization_rule: Use food/blood needs and social survival as stronger anchors than genre stereotypes.

canon_facts: Part of the undead threat; field writing notes that shadows can stalk victims invisibly and imitate them.
Baratheon is a rare shadow replacement.
safe_inferences: Identity theft, memory, fear and presence can shape unusual shadow speech.
shadow.knowledge_boundary: Do not give every shadow a fully articulate human biography.

canon_facts: A Revenant Skull can appear as the lesser haunting spawn of Curse Flesh.
It is also a temporary follower type.
safe_inferences: Very narrow identity centered on summoner/target and immediate task.
revenant_skull.knowledge_boundary_lift: No independent mortal biography unless deliberately elevated.

canon_facts: Rare replacement for Skeleton.
Compendium says he was an especially cruel mercenary captain responsible for mine security and slave discipline, earning the ironic nickname “Funny Bones.”
Carries Parashu and an eyepatch.
Funny Bones was an especially cruel mercenary captain responsible for mine security and slave discipline.
His fine equipment and stern demeanor earned him an ironic nickname.
safe_inferences: Cruel authoritarianism, mine-security experience, bitter irony and command habits.
He can plausibly retain command habits, punitive instincts, and a distorted sense of professional discipline after undeath.
funny_bones.knowledge_boundary: His exact mortal life beyond security/slave discipline is unknown.
funny_bones.individualization_rule: This is one of the strongest examples of a champion with an actual canon personality/history. Keep it fixed.

canon_facts: Ghoul hunter who rose to fame with a hunting posse.
His party was killed and sextons feared he would rise again.
Now an elite Enslaved Ghoul variant accompanied by three Ghouls.
Coral Grimes was a famous ghoul hunter whose posse rose to fame.

safe_inferences: Former hunter identity, command habits, irony of becoming what he hunted.

coral_grimes.knowledge_boundary: Do not invent his pre-hunter childhood or exact cause of transformation. Do not invent the exact circumstances of his party's death.
coral_grimes.individualization_rule: The hunter-to-ghoul reversal is central and canonically grounded.

canon_facts: Enigmatic master of the Hunters' Guild.
Disappeared investigating the undead surge and apparently became the vampire in Bram's Castle.
Bram Kindly is the enigmatic master of the Hunters' Guild.
He disappeared while investigating a surge in undead activity and appears to have become a vampire.
He resides in a personal room at the top of Bram's Castle.
safe_inferences: Professional investigator, former anti-undead specialist, now predator; conflict between duty and hunger.
His speech can plausibly blend hunter professionalism, investigative habits, and predatory self-awareness.
bram_kindly.knowledge_boundary: Do not invent how the transformation occurred unless later canon establishes it. Do not invent his pre-Guild childhood or exact method of vampiric transformation.
bram_kindly.individualization_rule: His former identity and castle situation must persist across every interaction.

canon_facts: Banished to the Underworld for betraying fellow Eternals.
Uses ghostly abilities and a magical bow.
Artemisia was banished to the Underworld for betraying her fellow Eternals.
She retains her magical bow in undeath and uses mimicry, levitation and teleportation.
safe_inferences: Exile, betrayal, resentment, self-reliance and survival.
Betrayal, exile and hunter-like cunning are direct characterization anchors.
artemisia.knowledge_boundary: Do not import external Artemisia mythology. The source does not define the exact nature of the betrayal; do not invent a specific treachery.
artemisia.individualization_rule: Her relationship to the Eternals and exile should be the core backstory.

canon_facts: Rare replacement for Shadow.
Drops an unusually large amount of gold compared with ordinary Shadows.
Baratheon is a rare Shadow replacement, visually distinct and level 50-51.
Baratheon drops a Phantom Mask.
Shadows are neutral with all denizens besides Humans and normally hostile to players unless using Spooky Mask.
safe_inferences: A more individualized/valuable shadow with status or accumulated possession.
He can be treated as an unusually formidable shadow with shadow-like identity confusion, but not given a fabricated human past.
baratheon.knowledge_boundary: No reliable biography currently established beyond the champion identity.
baratheon.individualization_rule: Use mystery and shadow psychology; do not fabricate history.

canon_facts: Playable demonic race associated with charm, teleportation, polymorph and social manipulation.
The Compendium describes succubi as crafty/cruel but notes some may pursue independent paths.
safe_inferences: Social perception, manipulation, independence and curiosity.
succubus.knowledge_boundary: Do not reduce every conversation to sexual themes or external demonology.
succubus.individualization_rule: Use social strategy as a broad capability, then individualize motive.

canon_facts: Verona, Aleera and Marishka are three named Succubus Consorts in Bram’s Castle.

They pledged themselves to a powerful vampire who tutored them in vampiric magic.
safe_inferences: Their relationship to the vampire, court-like status, loyalty and individualized feelings about that pact.
Model these three as a small social unit with shared tutelage rather than three unrelated succubi.
succubus_consort.knowledge_boundary: Treat their names and role as canon; personal histories beyond that remain open. Do not automatically identify their mentor as Bram Kindly unless another source establishes that; the page only says a powerful vampire.
succubus_consort.individualization_rule: Give each consort a distinct stance toward vampiric service without changing the shared backstory.

canon_facts: Playable demonic race related to succubi with its own abilities and social standings.
safe_inferences: Competition, intimidation, charm, territorial status.
incubus.knowledge_boundary: External incubus mythology is not Barony canon.
incubus.individualization_rule: Use role/class and personal ambition to differentiate individuals.

canon_facts: Common Hell-associated demon that can be summoned.
Occurs throughout Hell and as summoned combat support.
safe_inferences: Petty ambition, service to stronger demons, mischief and survival.
imp.individualization_rule: Short, opportunistic personalities; elevate only exceptional individuals.
imp.knowledge_boundary_lift: No broad infernal hierarchy unless source-supported.

canon_facts: Common Hellspawn associated with Herx/Baphomet and Hell.
Demons can be summoned and appear in the Ruins/Hell.
safe_inferences: Rank, task, loyalty and rivalry among demons.
demon.knowledge_boundary: Do not assume a universal Hell religion or hierarchy from generic demon encounters.

canon_facts: Rare Succubus replacement.

Can charm and teleport; carries charm magic staffs and roses.
Lilith is a title sometimes granted to succubi who lead and inspire other succubi.

safe_inferences: Leadership, influence, social confidence and manipulation.
Leadership through charisma, persuasion and manipulation is strongly supported.
lilith.knowledge_boundary: The title is cultural lore, but do not import external Lilith mythology.

canon_facts: Level 30 demon champion that can replace demons.
Compendium says he founded a vicious fraternity and is surrounded by demonic sycophants.
Uses fireball magic.
Deu De Breau founded a vicious demonic fraternity.

safe_inferences: Cult-like leadership, vanity, status obsession and manipulative hierarchy.
Status-conscious, cult-like leadership and abusive hierarchy are safer than generic demon personality.

canon_facts: Magical mechanical beings with boiler/heat systems and consciousness/essence mechanics.

canon_facts: Construct denizen associated with magical/crystal environments.

Citadel guardian/material logic is safer than inventing a crystal-golem civilization.

canon_facts: Construct built around sentry/security function.

canon_facts: Magic-oriented construct denizen.

canon_facts: Denizen explicitly described as a mimic and non-recruitable special monster.

skeleton_sentinel.knowledge_boundary: No independent mortal biography by default.

method: Official Barony Wiki denizen pages first.
Current Denizens roster second to verify entity existence, replacement/spawn behavior, and special-variant classification.
Dungeon Progression to establish location/ecology context.
Compendium excerpts reproduced on official denizen pages for individual characterization.
Mechanics used only for behavior/role inference, never as proof of biography.
important_corrections: The current Denizens page distinguishes eight non-Compendium/special entries: Goblin Shaman, Cockatrice (lair), Kobold Cultist, Skeleton Vanguard, Ghoul Chef, Skeleton Knight, Skeleton Sentinel, and Gyrobot.

Succubus Consorts are a named special group of three: Verona, Aleera, and Marishka; they should be modeled as three known individuals sharing a common canon relationship rather than as one generic consort type.
Bram Kindly is explicitly the enigmatic master of the Hunters Guild who disappeared investigating the undead surge; the source does not establish a detailed pre-undead biography.
Artemisia is explicitly an Eternal banished to the Underworld for betraying fellow Eternals.
Coral Grimes is explicitly a famous ghoul hunter whose party died; the Compendium frames his resurrection as feared because his old compulsions may persist.
Funny Bones is explicitly a cruel mercenary captain responsible for mine security and slave discipline.
Thumpus is explicitly respected by gnomes and accompanied by gnomes who follow him; this is stronger than our previous generic "troll champion" treatment.
Algernon is explicitly a very smart rat king created by a food boom, with six follower rats and a strong food/pack identity.
Skrabblag is explicitly associated with scorpion longevity/possible immortality claims; this is a naturalist claim, not established metaphysical fact.
Xyggi has a stated full name and is rumored by sorcerers to possess exceptional intellect because they believe intellect is born of magic.
Gharbad is a silver-furred goatman who attracts loyal followers; this provides a canon social-status hook.
Lilith is explicitly a title granted to succubi who lead and inspire others; the source says foes may switch sides under her influence.
Deu De Breau is explicitly founder of a vicious demonic fraternity and travels with demonic sycophants.
Shelob is explicitly presented as a possibly demonic spirit in spider form and leads three spiders; the Compendium phrasing is intentionally hearsay/claim, not objective fact.
Cockatrice Lair is an explicitly different, indomitable level-50 cockatrice confined to the Lair rather than an ordinary regional variant.
Gyrobot is explicitly a tinkering-built friendly construct whose quality determines its functions; it is not a wild NPC species.

relationship_knowledge_graph.purpose: Represent canonical social relationships separately from inferred links and control how knowledge propagates into NPC prompts. The graph is a grounding layer, not a source of invented biography.

knowledge_propagation.default_scope: A generated NPC receives direct self-knowledge + base race/class knowledge + nearby/local graph knowledge + only source-backed world knowledge relevant to current conversation.

distance_rules.0: The NPC itself, current form, own memories, inventory, activity, direct relationships.
distance_rules.1: People/factions/places the NPC directly interacts with or has a strong occupational connection to.
distance_rules.2: Widely known local history and public rumors; only inject when conversation topic activates them.
distance_rules.3_plus: Do not automatically propagate. Require explicit reason, book knowledge, specialist role, or witnessed event.

knowledge_propagation.relationship_memory: When NPC A establishes a relationship with NPC B during play, create a persistent memory edge; do not retroactively give NPC B reciprocal knowledge unless the relationship itself was shared or B already knew A.
knowledge_propagation.rumor_propagation: Rumors may travel through social encounters, but each hop downgrades confidence and preserves attribution (e.g. heard from a guild wizard, shopkeeper, goblin elder).
knowledge_propagation.secret_information: Secrets such as Archmagister plotting or precise infernal pact mechanics remain isolated until the player/NPC directly discovers them.
knowledge_propagation.witness_rule: A character can know an event through direct witnessing, a book, faction records, oral tradition, or rumor. Store the provenance so the NPC can answer in the appropriate voice.
knowledge_propagation.contradiction_rule: If two sources conflict or certainty is low, expose the disagreement in-character rather than resolving it silently.

dynamic_edges.description: Edges created during play rather than pre-authored. These are the main vehicle for emergent relationships.
dynamic_edges.persistence: Dynamic edges persist for the NPC/save and can influence trust, dialogue, future knowledge, and faction standing.

social_cluster_rules.purpose: Create depth without generating a 75-person fully connected graph.
rules: Give most ordinary social NPCs 0-3 persistent relationships.
Use canonical groups as anchors: goblin colonies, gnome colonies, Hunters Guild, Magicians Guild, ZAP Brigade, merchants, undead groups.
Create new relationships only when proximity, occupation, shared faction, family, or witnessed events justify them.
Prefer small local clusters per floor/settlement over global random connections.
Never overwrite a canonical edge with a generated edge.

runtime_example.forbidden_answer: Merchant confidently explains Merlin's secret resistance network or the Archmagisters' hidden plans unless the merchant has actually learned those secrets during play.

relationship_safety_rules.canonical_vs_inferred: Use source_type=direct only when the cited source explicitly establishes the relationship. Spawn adjacency, shared location, species affinity, or equipment similarity are not enough.
relationship_safety_rules.knowledge_vs_relationship: A knows fact X is not equivalent to A knows person B. Store knowledge separately from interpersonal edges.
relationship_safety_rules.formal_leadership: Use leads only when the source explicitly identifies followers/subordinates or the relationship is clearly organizational. Otherwise prefer accompanied_by, associated_with, respects, or may_follow.
relationship_safety_rules.rumor: Rumored/suspected relationships must retain attribution and uncertainty in runtime dialogue.
relationship_safety_rules.conditional_knowledge: Derived knowledge edges require a plausible trigger such as location, occupation, faction records, reading a book, direct witness, or conversation.
relationship_safety_rules.no_reciprocal_inference: A->B does not automatically imply B->A in knowledge or emotion. Reciprocal edges must be justified separately.
relationship_safety_rules.named_npc_priority: Named NPC canonical facts override generic race/group assumptions.

location_knowledge_audit.purpose: Audit and strengthen location-specific knowledge without assuming that spawning in a place automatically grants full historical or geographical knowledge. Location context should answer what an NPC can plausibly know because of residence, work, travel, repeated exposure, or direct observation.

rules.presence_is_not_mastery: An NPC being found in a region does not imply knowledge of its full history, secret passages, factions, or boss mechanics.
rules.resident_vs_visitor: Residents/workers receive stronger local knowledge. Visitors receive route/survival knowledge proportional to experience.
rules.secret_area_rule: Knowledge of a secret area should be treated as restricted unless the NPC has actually lived there, worked there, traveled there, read about it, or learned it from another source.
rules.procedural_floor_rule: For procedurally generated runs, location memories should attach to the realized floor/room and event history, not pretend the NPC knows a fixed map layout that may not exist in that seed.
rules.uncertainty_rule: When a location is poorly documented in canon, use sensory and practical knowledge rather than invented history.
rules.movement_rule: A character can gain new location knowledge through witnessed travel, repeated visits, books, employment, escort, or party history; this should be represented as dynamic memory rather than retroactive canon.

canon: The early dungeon is the Mines, strongly associated with mining, workers, traps, rats, spiders, skeletons, trolls and goblins.
Floor 2 always has an entrance to the Gnomish Mines unless generation fails; floor 3 has a 50% Minetown entrance; floor 5 can hide an Underworld portal.
high_value_local_knowledge: routes to secret entrances if actually discovered
restricted_knowledge: exact seeded map layout before exploration
npc_rules: A miner may know practical mining details without knowing Hamlet history.
A random rat knows immediate routes/food/threats, not the economy.
A survivor-family NPC may know the history of Herx only if learned from family/community tradition.

restricted_knowledge_never.exact seeded map layout before explorati: You have walked only the parts of these mines you have actually walked. The rest of the layout is unknown to you.
restricted_knowledge_never.hidden portals not personally discovered: You have never found a hidden portal yourself. Where any of them lie, you do not know.
restricted_knowledge_never.deep Guild or Herx secrets: Nobody of the Guild, and nobody of Herx's, ever trusted you with anything deep. Those secrets are unknown to you.

canon: A fixed maze-like secret area entered from floor 2.
Contains Gnomes, Trolls, substantial gold, an artifact, a shop, and a recurring audible cue of picks striking rock.
Gnomes are most commonly found here; Thumpus can bring Gnomes outside this area.
high_value_local_knowledge: dangerous trap room if personally explored
npc_rules: Gnome residents should have strong colony/resource knowledge.
Trolls can have territory knowledge without sharing Gnome social assumptions.
A Gnome encountered elsewhere should not automatically know the full mine layout.

restricted_knowledge_lifts.other secret areas: if the NPC has a personal connection to them

restricted_knowledge_never.other secret areas: You have never travelled to the other secret places below. You have no idea what is in them.
restricted_knowledge_never.full world history: Nobody ever taught you the history of the world. Most of it is simply blank to you.
restricted_knowledge_never.Archmagister plans: You have never had dealings with the Archmagisters. What they are planning, you do not know.

canon: Minetown is a secret human settlement with a 50% chance to generate from floor 3.
It is peaceful and contains several shops, Humans, recruitable NPCs, and local routines.
Its inhabitants descend from survivors/descendants of Hamlet and its society is ordinary underground life rather than a combat zone.
npc_rules: A Minetown merchant is a strong candidate for broad practical rumors because of customer traffic, but knowledge remains individual.

restricted_knowledge_lifts.Crystal Cave operations: if the NPC personally learned them

restricted_knowledge_never.Crystal Cave operations: You have never worked the Crystal Caves and nobody explained them to you. How they run is a blank to you.
restricted_knowledge_never.deep Magician Guild secrets: You have never been inside the Magician Guild's confidence. Their deeper business is unknown to you.
restricted_knowledge_never.secret boss mechanics: You have never faced what guards the hidden places, and you do not know how such a fight goes.

authoring_notes: Do not make every resident a direct descendant of a specific survivor or an anti-Herx zealot.
Minetown knowledge should feel communal but not omniscient.

canon: The Swamp is a major early region after the Mines.
It has strong Goblin presence and contains secret areas including the Temple and Haunted Castle.
A rare Goblin Shaman setpiece occurs here; Succubi also have a specific setpiece encounter here.
npc_rules: Goblin NPCs should have unusually strong Swamp familiarity when Swamp-born.
A Goblin elsewhere should not automatically know every Swamp secret.
Succubus encounter knowledge can be local and social rather than universal infernal knowledge.

restricted_knowledge_lifts.the Temple's internal layout: if the NPC has been inside
restricted_knowledge_lifts.Haunted Castle secrets: if the NPC has been there

restricted_knowledge_never.the Temple's internal layout: You have never once set foot inside the Temple. You have seen it only from the outside, and you have no idea what is in there.
restricted_knowledge_never.Haunted Castle secrets: You have never been inside the Haunted Castle. Whatever it hides, you have no idea what it is.
restricted_knowledge_never.later-region politics: You have never been deep enough to learn how power is arranged further down. Those politics are unknown to you.

canon: The Temple is a secret level reached from the Swamp.
It contains caged Trolls and Goblins, gates, traps, and a Green Mystic Orb.
The area has meaningful interactions involving releasing one group or another.
high_value_local_knowledge: the choice/interaction structure if personally experienced
npc_rules: NPCs can describe it as an abandoned/hostile set-piece if that is what they personally experienced.

restricted_knowledge_lifts.its exact layout: if the NPC has been inside

restricted_knowledge_never.its exact layout: You have never explored this place. You could not describe its plan to anyone.
restricted_knowledge_never.Temple existence before discovery: You could not have told anyone this place was here before it was found.

authoring_notes: Do not treat the Temple as a major religious institution merely because it is called a temple.

canon: The Haunted Castle is a secret level from the Swamp.
It is associated with undead/castle hazards and contains an artifact.
The broader late-game vampire/undead ecology connects it thematically to Bram's Castle, but they are separate locations.
npc_rules: A low-ranking undead can know its duty and rooms without knowing the castle's entire history.

restricted_knowledge_lifts.Bram Kindly's true identity: if the NPC personally learned it

restricted_knowledge_never.Bram Kindly's true identity: Nobody has ever told you who Bram Kindly really is. You genuinely do not know.
restricted_knowledge_never.Bram's Castle history: You have never learned the history of Bram's Castle. Its past is unknown to you.
restricted_knowledge_never.full late-game undead politics: You have never been party to how the undead powers arrange themselves. Their politics are beyond you.

authoring_notes: Do not collapse Haunted Castle and Bram's Castle into one place.

canon: The Labyrinth is an ancient, trap-heavy region and its supposed Xaz'Cetian history is explicitly uncertain in The Meaning of the Labyrinth.
It has unusual secret-route structure including Sokoban and the Minotaur Maze.
Goblins occur here, but they are much less common than in the Swamp.
high_value_local_knowledge: what the NPC has personally seen
npc_rules: Scholars may discuss Xaz'Cetian theories, but should identify them as theories.
A common monster should not speak like an archaeologist.

restricted_knowledge_lifts.the exact maze solution: if the NPC has solved it

restricted_knowledge_never.the exact maze solution: You have never solved this maze. You could not give anyone the way through.
restricted_knowledge_never.confirmed Xaz'Cetian history: No one has ever given you a settled account of the Xaz'Cetians. Their history is unknown to you.
restricted_knowledge_never.unseen ancient settlements: You have never travelled out to the old settlements. What became of them, you do not know.

authoring_notes: Minotaur-specific knowledge should be separated from general Labyrinth knowledge.

canon: Sokoban is an optional secret area reached from the Labyrinth progression and is treated as a puzzle/treasure location.

restricted_knowledge_never.existence before discovery: You could not have told anyone this place existed before you stumbled into it.
restricted_knowledge_never.solution paths without experience: You have never worked out the way through here. The solution is not something you hold.

authoring_notes: A puzzle-solving NPC may have learned habits, but do not grant universal knowledge of the puzzle solution.

canon: The Minotaur Maze is a dedicated secret level where the Minotaur always spawns.
The Minotaur receives special buffs in the maze; removing Gungnir from its pedestal strips most of those buffs and applies temporary Slow/Hungover.
The ZAP Brigade can appear on Minotaur floors and wait to fight it.
local_population: other local denizens according to generation
high_value_local_knowledge: Gungnir pedestal and effects if personally discovered
escape routes and Daedalus Shrine if personally seen
npc_rules: A Minotaur can know its territory and immediate pursuers without knowing the player-wide dungeon map.
A Brigadier knows Brigade objectives; a random NPC does not.

restricted_knowledge_lifts.the Minotaur countdown rules: if the NPC observed or was taught them

restricted_knowledge_never.the Minotaur countdown rules: You have never watched the maze's hunt from start to finish. You do not know how its timing works.
restricted_knowledge_never.ZAP/Merlin conspiracy as fact: You have never seen anything that proves a dealing between ZAP and Merlin. Whether it is real, you do not know.

canon: The Ruins are an ancient-city region with broad spaces and Magic Pillar traps.
They contain Gnomes, Gnome Thieves, Bugbears, Demons, Goblins, Skeleton setpieces, young Vampires, Spellbots, Sentrybots and neutral Automatons.
The Mystic Library is accessed from the Ruins; a portal in the second Ruins segment leads toward the Underworld/Hell route.
npc_rules: Ruins residents can have more cosmopolitan monster knowledge because many species coexist here, but not universal scholarship.
Automatons may know Citadel-related details only if their history supports it.

restricted_knowledge_lifts.Archmagister endgame plans: if the NPC was personally exposed to them

restricted_knowledge_never.Archmagister endgame plans: You have never been near an Archmagister's private counsel. What they intend is a blank to you.
restricted_knowledge_never.full ancient-city history: Nobody ever taught you what this city was. Its history is largely blank to you.
restricted_knowledge_never.Xaz'Cetian identity as fact: You have never seen anything that settles who or what the Xaz'Cetians were. You do not know.

canon: The Mystic Library is a late-game secret area accessed from the Ruins.
It is a major source of spellbooks, magic staffs and scrolls.
Access requires navigating the surrounding hazards and often levitation.
restricted_knowledge: specific books or contents not actually read
full Citadel/Archmagister secrets merely because the library exists
npc_rules: A scholar may know the Library by reputation; that is not the same as having visited it.

restricted_knowledge_never.specific books or contents not actually: You have read only the books you have actually read. What is written in the rest is unknown to you.
restricted_knowledge_never.full Citadel/Archmagister secrets merely: Standing among these books has taught you nothing of the Citadel's secrets. You do not know them.

canon: The Underworld is an unusual layer of islands over a huge pit and can be reached through more than one route.
It is traversed through levitation-friendly terrain and obelisks that teleport travelers between islands.
Depending on entry and exploration, the player can return to different dungeon floors or reach Hell.
Ghouls, Enslaved Ghouls, Imps, Skeletons, Humans, Shadows and Slimes appear here; Artemisia is encountered on the second Underworld.

restricted_knowledge_lifts.facts about Artemisia: if the NPC encountered her or was told
restricted_knowledge_lifts.details about Baphomet: if the NPC learned them from a source

restricted_knowledge_never.facts about Artemisia: You have never met Artemisia and nobody has told you about her. She is a name to you and nothing more.
restricted_knowledge_never.details about Baphomet: You have never had a reliable account of Baphomet from anyone. What is true of it, you do not know.
restricted_knowledge_never.Hell route before discovering it: You have never found the way down into Hell. Where that route lies, you do not know.

authoring_notes: Because the Underworld is non-linear and can be entered from multiple points, location knowledge should record which Underworld segment an NPC actually experienced.

canon: Hell is reached from the second Underworld route and occupies levels 21-24 in the current progression.
It is lava-filled and populated by Imps and Demons; Baphomet waits at the end of the route.
Baphomet is secretive and is only plausibly known to specialists, infernal creatures, direct witnesses, or characters with a specific information path.
high_value_local_knowledge: infernal hierarchy at the level personally witnessed
npc_rules: An Imp can know who commands it without knowing all infernal cosmology.
A generic human should not casually know precise Hell geography.
sources: The Adventurer Who Went To Hell

restricted_knowledge_never.precise pact mechanics: You have never seen a pact struck, and nobody has explained one to you. How they truly work, you do not know.
restricted_knowledge_never.Baphomet motives: Baphomet has never confided anything to you. What drives it, you do not know.
restricted_knowledge_never.Hell geography beyond actual travel: You know only the ground you have actually walked here. Beyond that, the shape of Hell is unknown to you.

canon: Lich's Bastion is the floor 20 boss area where Herx is fought.
After Herx, his magic sphere opens the portal to Hamlet.
high_value_local_knowledge: Herx encounter behavior and arena hazards only for direct witnesses/participants
restricted_knowledge: Herx's private motives beyond established canon

restricted_knowledge_never.exact arena mechanics before encounter: You have never watched what happens in that chamber. How a fight there goes, you do not know.
restricted_knowledge_never.Herx's private motives beyond establishe: Herx never confided in you. What he truly wants, beyond what everyone says, you do not know.

authoring_notes: Do not make ordinary dungeon NPCs know the Bastion layout merely because Herx is famous.

canon: Hamlet is reached after the Baron/Baphomet sequence and functions as a major hub with merchants, hirelings and a Magician's Guild outpost.
It is home to a small population of stronger Humans and is the staging ground for the Crystal Caves.
npc_rules: Hamlet residents can be unusually well-informed without becoming omniscient.
Guild staff may know Guild policy without knowing private Archmagister actions.

restricted_knowledge_never.Archmagister secret plans before disclos: Nobody has disclosed the Archmagisters' plans to you. What they intend, you do not know.
restricted_knowledge_never.Baphomet details beyond public rumor: Everything you have heard about Baphomet is common talk in the street. Beyond that you know nothing.

canon: The Crystal Caves are the next major layer after Hamlet and lead to Orpheus and Erudyce.
They contain Insectoids, Kobolds, Incubi, Cockatrices, Crystal Golems and Scarabs, with Xyggi as a rare Scarab replacement.
The caves are associated with the Magician's Guild, the Archmagisters and a major power struggle.
restricted_knowledge: exact cave secrets without direct experience
npc_rules: A Kobold resident may know more about local caves than a Guild mage.
A Guild mage may know institutional history but not every tunnel.

restricted_knowledge_never.Archmagister secret plans before exposur: No Archmagister has ever exposed their plans to you. What they are working toward, you do not know.
restricted_knowledge_never.exact cave secrets without direct experi: You have been only where your own feet have carried you here. The deeper secrets of these caves are unknown to you.

authoring_notes: Xyggi should not be treated as a universal spokesperson for Scarabs.

canon: Cockatrice Lair is a distinct secret floor reached late in the game and contains a unique higher-level Cockatrice variant that can only be found there.
The current denizen guide classifies the Lair Cockatrice as a distinct type and non-recruitable.
local_population: Kobold Cultists and setpiece inhabitants according to current taxonomy
high_value_local_knowledge: local cult/setpiece context if actually experienced

restricted_knowledge_never.existence/layout before discovery: You could not have told anyone this place was here before it was found, and you do not know its full extent.
restricted_knowledge_never.universal Kobold religion: You have never been shown any one faith that all kobolds share. Whether such a thing exists, you do not know.

authoring_notes: Treat Lair inhabitants as locally specialized, not as representatives of all Cockatrices or all Kobolds.
