event_memory_world_state.purpose: Turn player actions and major world changes into persistent, scoped memories and world-state facts that can propagate through relationships, locations, factions, and rumor channels without making NPCs omniscient.
event_memory_world_state.core_model: event -> immutable event record -> world-state facts -> observer-specific memories -> rumor/knowledge propagation -> dialogue/action context
design_principles: The event record is authoritative for what actually happened.
A memory is a character's knowledge of an event, not the event itself.
Knowledge has provenance: witnessed, heard_from, inferred, read, system_known, or fabricated_guess.
Witnesses may know details that distant NPCs cannot know.
Rumors preserve uncertainty and may distort details; canon/world-state facts do not.
Major world-state changes persist for the run/save; local memories may fade or be summarized.
Generated NPC biography never overwrites canonical events.
A player transformation changes current state immediately but does not erase persistent identity or previous memories.
Deaths, betrayals, rescues, recruitment, theft, boss victories, discoveries, and faction changes are events, not just dialogue topics.

event_scopes.personal: Only the actor/target and directly involved NPCs need an immediate memory.
event_scopes.encounter: Everyone who directly witnesses the event or participates in the same encounter can remember it.
event_scopes.local: NPCs in the same settlement/area can learn it through sight, immediate aftermath, or local gossip.
event_scopes.regional: The event can travel through active trade, guild, colony, hunter, or adventurer networks.
event_scopes.faction: Members of a faction can receive a filtered version according to rank and information channels.
event_scopes.global: Reserved for world-defining events such as major boss deaths or permanent campaign-state changes.

memory_provenance.witnessed: Highest-confidence personal evidence. The NPC saw/heard the event directly.
memory_provenance.participated: The NPC was an actor or target in the event.
memory_provenance.told_by: A specific trusted relationship transmitted the information.
memory_provenance.read: Obtained from a book, note, report, sign, or other persistent text.
memory_provenance.faction_report: Received through an institution or organized group.
memory_provenance.rumor: Indirect information whose details may be uncertain.
memory_provenance.inferred: Reasoned from known facts rather than directly observed.
memory_provenance.system_known: Safe engine/world-state fact available to the service; should not imply the NPC personally knows it.
memory_provenance.fabricated_guess: Never use this provenance for factual NPC memory. It is a prompt failure state.

memory_structure.subject: What/whom the memory is about.
memory_structure.last_recalled: Last time it was retrieved into prompt context.
memory_structure.visibility: personal, encounter, local, regional, faction, global.

canonical_world_events.claim: Hamlet's citizens trapped Baron Herx in the mines after luring him there with a false promise of gold.
canonical_world_events.propagation: Old human families, Minetown/Hamlet residents, historians, miners, and Guild researchers can know versions of this. Non-humans need a plausible transmission route.

canonical_world_events.claim: Herx returned as a lich empowered through an infernal pact and unleashed monsters against Hamlet.
canonical_world_events.propagation: Human survivors and Guild members may know broad facts; pact details remain specialist/secret knowledge.

canonical_world_events.claim: Baron Herx is defeated; the player's route opens onward to Hamlet.
canonical_world_events.propagation: Once verified by engine state, this becomes campaign truth. NPCs receive only the version their social/location network can plausibly learn.

canonical_world_events.claim: Baphomet is defeated; the pact binding Herx's continued lich existence is forfeit and the player exits Hell toward Hamlet.
canonical_world_events.propagation: Rarely understood in full by ordinary NPCs; most receive a simpler rumor such as 'the devil is dead' or 'the adventurer escaped Hell.'

canonical_world_events.claim: The Archmagisters' hidden plans in the Crystal Caves become exposed to the player after the earlier boss sequence opens the path toward them.
canonical_world_events.propagation: Guild members should not automatically know everything the player knows; disclosure travels through witnesses, reports, and survivors.

player_arrival.trigger: Player enters a new location or settlement.
player_arrival.memories: Nearby NPCs may remember first sight; residents do not all immediately know the player's history.

first_meeting.trigger: Player and NPC establish first meaningful interaction.
first_meeting.memories: Store one compact relationship memory on each side.

conversation.memories: Only store durable facts or emotionally important impressions; do not save every line.

trade.memories: Shopkeeper may remember repeat customer, unusually generous purchase, bargain dispute, or suspicious behavior. Routine purchases should normally summarize rather than accumulate.

theft.trigger: Player steals or is caught stealing.
theft.memories: Victim remembers personally; nearby witnesses may remember 'the thief' without exact inventory unless observed.

shopkeeper_assault.trigger: Player directly harms a shopkeeper or is implicated in the incident.
shopkeeper_assault.memories: Immediate shop network remembers the attack. Persistent Wanted behavior follows engine state rather than AI judgment.

recruitment.memories: NPC remembers recruitment circumstances, initial trust, and commands received; leader remembers follower identity.

dismissal.trigger: Follower is dismissed or leaves the party.
dismissal.memories: Former follower retains relationship history unless their identity is otherwise lost.

follower_death.memories: Witnesses and close allies get high emotional-weight memories; distant NPCs learn only through later retelling.

npc_death.trigger: A named or persistent NPC dies.
npc_death.memories: Family/faction/local ties increase propagation; random wildlife generally does not receive abstract bereavement unless socially connected.

rescue.trigger: Player saves an NPC from danger.
rescue.memories: Rescued NPC receives strong personal gratitude/fear memory; their friends may hear a simplified account.

betrayal.trigger: NPC violates an established trust relationship.
betrayal.memories: Victim gets high emotional weight; the faction may receive a version depending on visibility.

book_read.memories: Reading does not globally teach NPCs. Nearby NPCs may know the player read a book if they observed it, but its contents propagate only if the player retells or the text is independently known.

location_discovered.trigger: Player enters a named or secret location for the first time.
location_discovered.memories: Discovery is strongest for the discoverer; information spreads through party members and later retellings.

boss_encountered.trigger: Player meets a boss or receives direct boss telepathy/dialogue.
boss_encountered.memories: Herx's direct telepathy is especially personal; do not give unrelated NPCs the exact text of what Herx told the player.

boss_defeated.memories: Party witnesses remember details; local inhabitants learn broad outcome; rumors may exaggerate.

polymorph.memories: Witnesses remember the transformation; current allegiance/form updates immediately; persistent identity stays unchanged.

major_item_acquired.trigger: Player acquires an unusual or plot-relevant item.
major_item_acquired.memories: Only witnesses or informed observers remember exact possession. NPCs do not magically inspect hidden inventory.

world_state_transition.memories: The state itself is authoritative; individual NPC knowledge still depends on propagation.

world_state_projection.principle: Maintain campaign truth separately from character knowledge.
world_state_projection.state_to_dialogue_rule: The AI may use a world-state fact only when the NPC has a justified knowledge path to it. Otherwise the fact stays engine-side.
world_state_projection.example: hamlet_unlocked=true does not mean every NPC knows who killed Herx; a Hamlet resident may know the aftermath, while a far-away cave creature may know nothing.

propagation_rules.same_party: Share the event with party members at near-witness confidence.
propagation_rules.same_household_or_close_relationship: Propagate a summarized account when contact occurs or a local report is received.
propagation_rules.same_location: Create local rumor only after a plausible time/transmission step; do not instant-broadcast.
propagation_rules.same_faction: Propagate through leadership/report channels when the faction has a reason to collect the information.
propagation_rules.merchant_network: Transactions and famous adventurer activity can travel regionally through trade gossip, but details degrade.
propagation_rules.guild_network: Scholarly/magical events can travel further than ordinary gossip if reported to the Guild.
propagation_rules.monster_colony: Use colony leader or raid/scout channels; individuals do not share all knowledge automatically.
propagation_rules.global: Only the world-state flag is global. Character memory remains individualized.

rumor_model.rule: Rumors are generated from one or more memories, never directly from the raw global event log.
rumor_model.anti_hallucination: Rumor language must not be used to smuggle invented facts into canon; the underlying claim must have a real source memory.
rumor_model.hard_rule: Every rumor must point to at least one originating memory or canonical public source.

memory_decay.routine: Summarize after repeated similar events instead of storing every instance.
memory_decay.notable: Keep indefinitely but compress wording after long intervals.
memory_decay.major: Keep indefinitely with exact identity/location if known.
memory_decay.world_changing: Never delete the underlying event; compress individual recollections while retaining the canonical event and relevant personal interpretations.
memory_decay.emotional: High emotional weight resists forgetting and should be preferentially recalled when relevant.
memory_decay.perishable: Exact prices, minor conversations, and incidental observations may decay quickly unless tied to relationship or conflict.

privacy_and_scope.inventory: NPCs do not know hidden player inventory unless observed, told, traded, or otherwise mechanically exposed.
privacy_and_scope.telepathy: Only canonical telepathic entities may directly access knowledge they could not otherwise observe; Herx is the explicit example.
privacy_and_scope.party_memory: Party members can share events by proximity/communication; do not assume all followers have identical private memories.
privacy_and_scope.death_memory: Death is not automatically globally announced.
privacy_and_scope.save_consistency: All persistent event records and world-state flags should serialize with the save; ephemeral prompt summaries can be regenerated.
privacy_and_scope.engine_state_boundary: The service may receive verified state from the engine, but an NPC must not be treated as knowing that state unless a knowledge path grants it.

runtime_prompt_builder.hard_cap_guideline: Inject 3-8 memories plus 0-3 world-state facts per conversation unless the NPC is a specialist with a legitimate broader context.
runtime_prompt_builder.memory_retrieval: Use semantic/event relevance, recency, emotional weight, relationship relevance, and location match. Never dump the entire event history.
runtime_prompt_builder.contradiction_resolution: If a personal memory conflicts with a world fact, preserve both as perspective: 'I saw X' vs 'the official report says Y'. Never overwrite a canonical engine fact with dialogue.

polymorph_in_town.shopkeeper_reaction: Use current engine allegiance plus remembered identity; do not erase prior interactions.

verified_facts: Herx can communicate telepathically with the player during descent.
Defeating Herx yields the Purple Mystic Orb and can open the portal to Hamlet.
Defeating Baphomet voids Herx’s pact and results in the player proceeding to Hamlet.
The Archmagisters remain unaware to ordinary Guild members while they operate in the Crystal Caves; the caves are sealed until Herx or Baphomet is defeated.
Orpheus and Erudyce have telepathy, but this does not imply access to player information they could not canonically observe.
Direct harm creates Wanted status and makes shopkeepers hostile; the status has engine-defined removal conditions.
Polymorph can change the player’s race and can clear Wanted status under the documented mechanics.
Leadership is an existing persistent follower system with commands and recruitment rules.

corrections: Event memories describe character knowledge, not objective world state. Engine-authoritative facts must remain separate from NPC knowledge.
Numerical confidence values in the previous version were removed from runtime semantics. Confidence is now categorical: direct/high, supported, plausible, rumor, unknown.
“Same party” propagation is no longer assumed to create identical memories; each party member receives an event only according to their actual observation/communication path.
Location and faction propagation are no longer immediate broadcasts. A transmission mechanism is required: witness, conversation, report, book, merchant contact, colony scout, etc.
Book reading is explicitly personal knowledge unless another character observes the reading or later learns the content.
Exact player inventory, hidden items, secrets, and private conversation content do not propagate without observation or disclosure.

Generic event categories such as faction_change, quest_like_goal_started, and quest_like_goal_completed are design placeholders rather than established Barony event types; they are marked proposal_only.
Gender/form transitions are treated as engine observations, not necessarily lore events. They affect memories only when an NPC actually witnesses or learns of the change.
World-changing events are not globally narrated verbatim. A global flag can become true while individual NPCs remain ignorant of who caused it or how it happened.
Rumor distortion can alter detail but may not create a new actor, motive, location, casualty, or outcome that is absent from the originating memory.

major_findings: The 14-race roster and 26-class roster are correct.
Several class personality descriptions were stronger than their evidence warranted and have been reframed as inference.
Scion's prior 'high-status' characterization was unsupported and has been removed.
Sexton is better characterized as a Church-affiliated temple officer and planner than as a generic funerary worker.
Insectoid social linkage was corrected to the explicitly listed standings (Insectoids, Scarabs, Scorpions, Automatons); Kobolds were removed from that canon claim.
Myconid and Salamander profiles were tightened to distinguish game mechanics from cultural psychology.
Race and class are now explicitly treated as evidence about mechanics/training/role, not deterministic personality.

race_class_personality_audit.remaining_policy: Do not promote any inferred personality trait to canon merely because it is repeated across generated NPCs.

context_resolution_audit.purpose: Define exactly how the runtime chooses which facts, memories, relationships, location knowledge, and book claims may enter one NPC prompt.
context_resolution_audit.core_principle: The runtime should retrieve the smallest sufficient context, not the largest available context.

authoritative_layers.engine_state: Current mutable game facts: current entity state, allegiance/hostility, location, floor, HP, inventory when intentionally exposed, current activity, and engine-confirmed world flags.
authoritative_layers.persistent_identity: Cached generated identity: name, generated background, stable personality, established relationships, durable personal memories.
authoritative_layers.canonical_lore: Source-backed Barony facts from books, official wiki/Compendium, and verified game data.
authoritative_layers.derived_knowledge: Knowledge an NPC plausibly acquired from relationships, location, profession, faction, books, observation, oral transmission, or rumor.
authoritative_layers.generation: New personal details created for one NPC. Generation may fill biography/personality gaps but cannot create objective historical facts.

topic_activation.rule: Do not inject every known fact into every conversation. Activate only facts relevant to the current subject or immediate situation.

evidence_requirements.canon_fact: Must have a source-backed canonical entry.
evidence_requirements.personal_memory: Must have an event/observation record tied to this NPC.
evidence_requirements.relationship_fact: Must have a canonical edge or a persistent dynamic relationship record.
evidence_requirements.book_knowledge: Must have a book-read or valid transmission record; book existence alone is insufficient.
evidence_requirements.location_knowledge: Must derive from residence, occupation, repeated travel, explicit teaching, direct observation, or another recorded acquisition path.
evidence_requirements.rumor: Must originate from an existing source memory and preserve attribution/uncertainty.
evidence_requirements.inference: May shape phrasing or personality but should not be asserted as objective history.

negative_knowledge.rule: Absence of an acquisition path is evidence against knowledge, not a blank to be filled.
runtime_behavior: If a fact has no source, return UNKNOWN.
If a fact is only plausible but not acquired, phrase it as speculation only when the NPC has a reason to speculate.
Never upgrade UNKNOWN to known merely because the fact is nearby in the lore file.
Never use another NPC's knowledge as the current NPC's knowledge without a transmission edge.

contradiction_handling.rule: When two acquired sources disagree, retain both claims with provenance instead of resolving them globally.
contradiction_handling.example: A Guild report may say the ZAP Brigade's Merlin connection is conjecture while a ZAP member may claim the Brigade has never heard of Merlin.
contradiction_handling.dialogue_behavior: The NPC should describe which source they trust and why.

context_budget.target_facts: 3-8 highly relevant facts/memories for an ordinary conversation.
context_budget.maximum: Avoid flooding the prompt with unrelated lore; additional context requires a demonstrated conversational reason.
context_budget.ordering: Recent/direct memories first; canonical constraints before inferred personality flavor.

special_entity_handling.bosses: Use authored canonical profiles and event state. Do not fallback to generic race/class biography generation.
special_entity_handling.named_champions: Use bespoke canon first; only fill genuinely unknown traits with clearly marked inference.
special_entity_handling.shopkeepers: Use current shop state, trading interaction history, customer history, location, and acquired local information. Do not assume omniscient merchant knowledge.
special_entity_handling.followers: Use personal relationship state, observed player actions, party relationships, current morale/trust variables if the social system has them, and canon role/lore.
special_entity_handling.trash_mobs: Use lightweight sensory/task context; do not inject the full knowledge graph.

race_class_guardrail.rule: Race and class are late-stage context modifiers, not primary knowledge sources.
race_class_guardrail.race: Use for known abilities, explicit social standings, and source-backed cultural context.
race_class_guardrail.class: Use for training, equipment, practiced behavior, institutional affiliation, and official flavor.
race_class_guardrail.personality: Use generated personality and life history to decide how the NPC interprets facts; do not let class/race dictate morality.

persistent_identity_vs_live_state.rule: A live state change does not rewrite persistent history; it changes the present-tense interpretation of the NPC.

relationship_graph_safety.knowledge_separation: Relationship edges, knowledge edges, memories, and current emotional state are separate data; none silently creates another.

shopkeeper_information_audit.core_principle: Shopkeepers are information-rich because of their profession and repeated contact with travelers, but they are not omniscient. Commercial access creates plausible information channels, not automatic knowledge.

verified_canonical_foundation.shop_role: Shopkeepers trade items for gold and operate specialized stores; most shops contain one or two shopkeepers.
verified_canonical_foundation.store_specialization: Each shop has a store type controlling what it buys and sells.
verified_canonical_foundation.trading_dialogue: Higher Trading skill changes shopkeeper dialogue toward a more begrudging/fair-trade tone.
verified_canonical_foundation.private_selection: Shops can have a private selection of up to four items whose access depends on Trading plus Charisma.
verified_canonical_foundation.merchant_class: The Merchant class is affiliated with the Merchant's Guild and has high Trading, Lore, and Charisma, supporting strong commercial/social expertise without implying universal knowledge.
verified_canonical_foundation.source_evidence: Shopkeeper Joe's Surviving the Mines demonstrates that a shopkeeper can possess practical monster knowledge and personal opinions, but also uses first-person uncertainty ('I think') for some claims.

safe_facts: what a customer bought or sold
direct_customer_interaction.guardrail: Do not infer hidden motives or unseen actions from a transaction alone.

merchant_network.guardrail: Every nonpublic claim needs a transmission/source record.

local_observation.guardrail: A shopkeeper only knows what their location and routine plausibly expose them to.

shop_inventory.guardrail: Inventory does not prove where an item came from or who previously owned it.

book_and_document_access.guardrail: Being a shopkeeper does not automatically grant knowledge of the global book corpus.

personal_experience.guardrail: Personal experience remains individual and should not become generic shopkeeper lore.

information_economy.free_information: Routine trade facts, obvious local observations, basic public gossip, and information the shopkeeper has little reason to protect.
information_economy.paid_information: Useful but noncritical rumors, route advice, customer histories, uncommon item information, and specialized practical knowledge.
information_economy.expensive_information: Privileged customer information, faction-sensitive rumors, dangerous routes, information that could materially endanger the shopkeeper, or information requiring trust.
refusal_conditions: information is too uncertain to sell confidently
NPC has an active grudge against the player
player has not established sufficient trust/payment
information_economy.uncertainty_rule: Selling information does not convert rumor into fact. The shopkeeper should preserve uncertainty and source attribution.

customer_memory.forgetting_rule: Minor one-off transactions should have low persistence and may be forgotten or compressed.
customer_memory.identity_rule: Recognizing a recurring customer requires a prior encounter or explicit identifying feature; a shopkeeper should not automatically recognize every adventurer.
customer_memory.privacy_rule: A customer transaction is private unless the shopkeeper has a reason/path to share it.

rumor_propagation.rule: Rumors propagate through explicit transmission edges, not through global world-state broadcast.
rumor_propagation.distortion: Each transmission may reduce certainty or alter wording without changing the underlying canonical fact.
rumor_propagation.canonical_protection: Rumors cannot overwrite canonical facts; they are stored as claims with provenance.
rumor_propagation.shopkeeper_advantage: Repeated commerce creates more opportunities for receiving rumors, so shopkeepers can have broader information breadth than ordinary NPCs without possessing deeper privileged knowledge.

shopkeeper_personality_axes.discretion: How carefully they protect customer/faction secrets.
shopkeeper_personality_axes.curiosity: How much they ask customers questions.
shopkeeper_personality_axes.territoriality: How protective they are of their shop and local area.
shopkeeper_personality_axes.loyalty: How strongly they protect particular customers/factions.
shopkeeper_personality_axes.risk_tolerance: How willing they are to share dangerous information.

critical_anti_leak_rules: Shopkeeper class or profession does not equal omniscience.
A shopkeeper does not automatically know everything that happened on the floor where their shop is located.
A customer purchase does not reveal the customer's quest, destination, or intentions.
A sold item does not reveal its full provenance unless the shopkeeper learned it.
Merchant Guild affiliation does not grant every Guild secret.
Knowing a rumor does not make it true.
Repeated customer traffic increases opportunities for knowledge acquisition but does not guarantee any specific rumor.
A shopkeeper can know more facts than an ordinary NPC while still having many UNKNOWN entries.
shopkeeper_information_audit.special_rule_for_joe: Surviving the Mines should be treated as evidence that Shopkeeper Joe possessed practical monster knowledge and opinions. Claims such as his theory that Goblins were devolved miners remain attributed to Joe rather than being promoted to objective canon.

communication_audit.scope: Communication, comprehension, and representation across the current Barony denizen taxonomy, with special attention to Rat/Spider/Arthropod communication and Shaman shapeshifting.

source_distinction.canon: Barony explicitly documents affinity/recruitment, shapeshift forms, quoted dialogue, and some special communication behavior.
source_distinction.project_inference: The game does not publish a complete language taxonomy for all denizens. Communication compatibility below is therefore a proposed immersion rule layered over canon.
source_distinction.implementation_rule: Never present a proposed communication channel as canon world history.

key_verified_findings: Rat Form lets the player recruit Rats; normal players are otherwise hostile to Rats.
Arthropod Form lets the player recruit Spiders, Scarabs, and Scorpions.
A true Insectoid can recruit Insectoids and is friendly with Scarabs and Scorpions; Arthropod Form specifically enables recruitment of Spiders, Scarabs, and Scorpions.
Shaman shapeshifts into Rat, Arthropod/Spider, Troll, and Imp forms, with each form changing friends and behavior.
Gnomes have distinct sounds; this supports audible creature signaling but does not establish a separate spoken language.
Herx has canonical telepathic communication with the player.
Baphomet is presented as essentially silent/nonverbal; preserve that authored exception.
Automatons are living constructs with consciousness in the Compendium, so semantic communication is a reasonable project rule, but a universal machine language is not established.
Many creatures have sound effects rather than documented dialogue; sounds must not be mistaken for semantic speech.

common_humanoid.guardrail: Do not claim Barony canonically documents one universal language for all humanoids; this is a communication convenience for the mod unless later source work establishes distinctions.

rat.canon_basis: Rat Form specifically changes hostility and permits Rat recruitment.

arthropod.canon_basis: Arthropod Form explicitly permits recruitment of Arthropods, Scarabs, and Scorpions.

troll.guardrail: Troll Form changes affinity and permits Troll recruitment; it does not explicitly document a Troll language.

imp.guardrail: Imp Form changes affinity and permits Imp recruitment; semantic dialogue is a project rule, not documented language canon.

undead_semantic.guardrail: Undead do not automatically share memories or a universal undead language.

demonic_semantic.guardrail: Baphomet is a special nonverbal exception.

construct_semantic.guardrail: Automaton consciousness supports semantic communication as a mod rule; do not assume every robot-like entity is conversational.

low_ontology.default_rendering: sounds, movement, posture, territorial behavior, hunger, sensory impressions
low_ontology.guardrail: This is an interface rule, not a claim that these creatures have no intelligence.

special_nonverbal.rendering: environmental manifestations, physical action, sound, supernatural effects, or authored nonverbal communication

player_interface_rules.semantic_conversation: Render ordinary translated dialogue only when the player has a compatible communication channel.
player_interface_rules.incompatible_animal: Render animal/creature sounds plus concise behavioral cues; the AI may internally model intent but must not output the semantic translation as if the human understood it.
player_interface_rules.compatible_animal_form: Render semantic dialogue from the creature perspective using its sensory priorities rather than human encyclopedic speech.
player_interface_rules.mixed_party: If a follower later serves as an interpreter, require an explicit social/knowledge event before translating animal knowledge to another party member.
player_interface_rules.reversion: Leaving a compatible animal form removes direct semantic access unless another active ability grants it.
player_interface_rules.memory: Communication compatibility affects transmission, not the NPC’s own memory.

animal_perspectives.guardrail: These are perspective priorities, not evidence of literal animal language or a fixed cognition scale.

special_cases.Anansi: Spider-associated mechanics do not make Anansi a Spider or automatically grant Spider-language access.
special_cases.Shaman: Shapeshifting is the strongest gameplay justification for changing communication channels because each form changes creature affinity/recruitment.
special_cases.Baphomet: Do not translate nonverbal boss behavior into ordinary dialogue.
special_cases.Herx: Telepathy is a canonical exception and permits semantic communication without ordinary shared speech.
special_cases.summoned_skeletons: Summoned status does not imply a unique mortal biography. Semantic speech should depend on the mod’s consciousness model and context.
special_cases.Gyrobot: Treat as a constructed companion with task/function communication unless the individual has generated speech capability.
special_cases.Mimic: Deception is separate from language; do not assume a universal mimic language.

anti_hallucination_rules: Do not claim Barony documents a universal Common language unless a source establishes it.
Do not invent an Animal Tongue canon spell or race ability.
Do not equate recruitment with proof of literal spoken language; use it as the strongest design signal for compatible communication.
Do not translate animal noises into semantic dialogue for an incompatible player.
Do not make every animal communicate like a small human.
Do not give every construct human-like speech.
Do not make every demon or undead share one language or memory pool.
Named NPC exceptions override generic defaults.
